Stalin’s speech emphasizes overcoming Russia’s historical backwardness to avoid being exploited or defeated by foreign powers.  
The German invasion of the Soviet Union in 1941 was a major test of Soviet industrial and military strength, which had been built up rapidly under Stalin’s industrialization drive in the 1930s.  
The Soviet Union’s ability to eventually repel the invasion, despite huge initial losses, could be seen as vindication of Stalin’s push for industrialization and military power.
